name: Roof Replacement
title: Roof Replacement in Knoxville, TN | Compare Free Quotes
meta_description: Get up to 3 free roof replacement quotes from licensed, insured Knoxville roofers. Compare shingle and metal options with no cost and no obligation to hire.
hero_subtitle: Describe your home once and hear from up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers with replacement quotes you can compare side by side. Free for homeowners, with no obligation.
intro: Knoxville roofs take on about 52 inches of precipitation in a normal year, a spring hail season and summers humid enough to grow dark algae streaks on shingles. When patching no longer keeps up, a full replacement resets the clock. This page explains what a tear-off involves, what 2026 Tennessee cost guides report for shingles and metal, which state license applies to your project, and how to line up competing quotes so you're comparing the same scope of work.

sections.heading: Signs it's time to replace instead of repair
body: Age is the first clue. InterNACHI's life-expectancy chart puts 3-tab asphalt shingles at roughly 20 years and architectural shingles at about 30, and it notes that heat and severe weather shorten those numbers. If your roof is in that range and you're seeing curled or cupped shingles, bald spots where granules have washed into the gutters, or more than one leak in a season, get a replacement price alongside a repair price.

Check the attic as well. Daylight showing through the boards, sagging decking, or water stains in several rooms usually point to problems that a handful of new shingles won't solve. Black streaks by themselves are a different matter: they're typically algae, which is mostly cosmetic, so don't let anyone sell you a new roof on streaks alone.

sections.heading: What a full replacement involves
body: Most asphalt re-roofs start with a tear-off down to the wood deck. The crew inspects the decking and swaps out soft or rotted sheets, then installs underlayment, ice-and-water membrane in valleys and around penetrations, new drip edge, flashing at walls and chimneys, the shingles, and ridge vents or other exhaust ventilation. Deck replacement is often priced per sheet because nobody can see its condition until the old roof is off.

Steep, cut-up rooflines take more labor. Modernize's Tennessee cost guide notes that steeper rooflines and older homes add labor time in Knoxville, and that moisture management and attic ventilation are especially important in East Tennessee's variable climate. A replacement is the right time to fix an attic that runs hot or damp.

sections.heading: Choosing a material for East Tennessee
body: Architectural, or dimensional, shingles are the usual choice on re-roofs today. They cost a little more than 3-tab and carry a longer expected life. In a humid valley climate, ask for shingles with algae-resistant granules; the Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association says copper in those granules helps block the Gloeocapsa magma algae behind most dark streaking.

Metal costs more up front, but InterNACHI estimates 40 to 80 years of service. Standing seam with concealed fasteners sits at the top of the price range, while exposed-fastener panels cost less but have screws and washers that need periodic attention. If you expect to stay in the house for decades, price both.

sections.heading: Licensing and paperwork in Knox County
body: Tennessee requires a state contractor's license before anyone bids or negotiates a project of $25,000 or more. Knox County is also one of nine Tennessee counties where a Home Improvement license is required for residential projects from $3,000 to $24,999, and the state lists roofing as covered work. Blount, Sevier, Anderson and Loudon counties are not on that list, so the rules change a few miles from downtown.

Whatever the price, look the contractor up on the state's license search at search.cloud.commerce.tn.gov before you sign. The Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance (TDCI) also notes that state law limits deposits on home improvement projects to one-third of the contract price.

sections.heading: How to compare replacement quotes
body: Line the bids up item by item: shingle brand and product line, underlayment type, whether a full tear-off is included, the per-sheet price for decking, new flashing versus reused flashing, ventilation changes, debris haul-off, and who handles any required permit. A low number that leaves out decking or flashing isn't really low.

Then compare warranties. Manufacturer coverage on materials is separate from the roofer's workmanship warranty, and workmanship terms vary a lot from one contractor to the next. Get both in writing, along with a start window and a payment schedule tied to progress.

cost_table.caption: Installed roof replacement costs reported in 2026 guides. Rough ranges per square foot of roof area, not quotes.
rows: $11,500–$20,000 for a 2,000 sq ft roof in the Knoxville area
$22,000–$40,000 for a 2,000 sq ft roof in Tennessee

checklist: Look up the license at search.cloud.commerce.tn.gov and confirm the business name matches the contract
Ask for proof of general liability and workers' compensation insurance
Confirm whether the price is for a full tear-off or an overlay
Get the per-sheet price for replacing damaged decking in writing
Ask which shingle line is quoted and whether it has algae-resistant granules
Ask who pulls any required permit and schedules inspections
Get the workmanship warranty in writing, separate from the manufacturer warranty
Keep the deposit at or below one-third of the contract price

faqs.q: How much does a roof replacement cost in Knoxville?
faqs.a: Modernize's 2026 Tennessee guide lists $11,500 to $20,000 to replace a 2,000 square foot roof with architectural shingles in the Knoxville area. Roof area is larger than floor area: HomeAdvisor estimates a roof at roughly 1.1 to 1.2 times a home's square footage. Pitch, layers to remove, decking condition and material all move the final number, so local quotes are the only way to pin it down.

faqs.q: How long will a new roof last in East Tennessee?
faqs.a: InterNACHI estimates about 20 years for 3-tab shingles, about 30 for architectural shingles and 40 to 80 for metal. It also notes that hot weather and severe storms such as hail can shorten a roof's life. Good attic ventilation, clean gutters and prompt repairs after storms help a roof reach the long end of its range.

faqs.q: Can new shingles go over my old ones?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but a tear-off lets the crew inspect and repair the deck, replace worn flashing and install fresh underlayment, which an overlay skips. Ask each roofer which method they're quoting and why, and whether an overlay is allowed on your house. Comparing a tear-off bid with an overlay bid isn't a fair comparison.

faqs.q: Does my roofer need a license in Knox County?
faqs.a: For residential work from $3,000 to $24,999 in Knox County, Tennessee requires a Home Improvement license, and roofing is listed as covered work. Projects of $25,000 or more need a state contractor's license. You can check either one on the state's search site, search.cloud.commerce.tn.gov, before you sign anything.

faqs.q: Is it really free to request quotes?
faqs.a: Yes. Homeowners pay nothing to request quotes and are under no obligation to hire any of the roofers who contact them. Local contractors pay for the referral. You'll hear from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers, who usually reach out within 24 to 48 hours.

name: Roof Repair
title: Roof Repair in Knoxville, TN | Free Quotes from Roofers
meta_description: Need a roof leak fixed or shingles replaced in Knoxville? Request free repair quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers. No cost, no obligation.
h1: Roof Repair Quotes in Knoxville, TN
hero_subtitle: Tell us about the leak or damage and get matched with up to 3 licensed, insured Knoxville-area roofers who handle repairs. Free to request, with no obligation to hire.
intro: Most roofs don't fail all at once. A cracked pipe boot, a few shingles torn loose in a summer thunderstorm, or flashing pulling away from a chimney can let water in years before the rest of the roof wears out. On a roof that's otherwise sound, a well-done repair is usually the most economical choice. This page covers the repairs Knoxville homeowners run into most, what national cost guides report, when a repair stops making sense, and how to keep a small job from turning into an upsell.

sections.heading: Common repairs on Knoxville homes
body: Leaks usually start where the roof surface is interrupted: plumbing vent boots whose rubber collars crack in the sun, step flashing where a roof meets a sidewall, chimney flashing and counterflashing, skylight curbs, and valleys that carry heavy runoff. With Knoxville averaging close to 52 inches of precipitation a year under National Weather Service normals, those weak spots get tested often.

Wind is the other regular cause. The NWS office in Morristown found that damaging thunderstorm winds become the dominant type of severe weather in June and through the summer. Lifted or missing shingles after a storm are usually a repair job, as long as the surrounding shingles still seal down and the deck underneath is dry.

sections.heading: Signs a repair can't wait
body: Water spots on a ceiling, damp insulation in the attic, a musty smell after rain, or shingle pieces in the yard all justify a call. So do granules piling up below the downspouts on a roof that isn't that old, and nail heads that have backed out and are lifting shingle tabs.

Freeze-thaw plays a part too. Knoxville averages about 68 nights a year at or below freezing over the NWS period of record, so moisture that gets into a cracked sealant joint or a loose flashing seam can freeze and widen the gap over a winter. Fixing it in the fall costs less than chasing a ceiling stain in March.

Dark streaks running down the slopes are not, by themselves, a repair call. The Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association identifies them as algae, mainly Gloeocapsa magma, which thrives in warm, humid conditions like a Knoxville summer. ARMA also warns against pressure washing a shingle roof, since it can strip away the protective granules.

sections.heading: What a proper repair includes
body: A good roofer finds the source, not just the wet spot. Water can run along rafters or decking before it drips, so the fix belongs at the point of entry, and the roofer should be able to show it to you in photos. Replacement shingles should be matched as closely as practical, nailed to the manufacturer's pattern and sealed down.

Ask how flashing will be handled. Smearing roof cement over a failed flashing joint can stop a drip for a season, but replacing the flashing or the pipe boot is the lasting fix. If the decking under the repair area is soft, it should be cut out and replaced before new shingles go on.

sections.heading: Repair or replace?
body: Repair generally makes sense when the damage is limited to one area and the rest of the roof has years left. When shingles are brittle across every slope, granule loss is widespread, or a new leak shows up somewhere different each year, the money may be better spent on replacement. Asking one contractor for both prices gives you a useful comparison.

Color matching is another factor. Shingle colors and product lines get discontinued, so a patch on an aging roof may never blend in. That's cosmetic rather than structural, but it can matter if you plan to sell soon.

sections.heading: Keeping a small job small
body: Most roofers are straightforward, but a repair visit is also a sales opportunity. If someone says the whole roof has to go, ask for photos of each problem and a plain explanation of why a repair won't hold. A second opinion from another contractor costs you only a little time.

Licensing depends on the price. In Knox County, a repair priced between $3,000 and $24,999 requires the contractor to hold a state Home Improvement license; for smaller jobs, TDCI suggests checking with your local codes office about any local license. Get the scope and price in writing before work starts, whatever the size, and follow TDCI's advice to put the payment terms in writing too.

cost_table.caption: National roof repair costs reported by HomeAdvisor (updated June 2026). Rough ranges, not quotes.
rows: Repair of a 100 sq ft area

checklist: Ask the roofer to show you photos of the leak source, not just the ceiling stain
Confirm whether flashing or pipe boots will be replaced or only resealed
Ask which replacement shingle will be used and how closely it will match
Get a price for replacing any soft decking found under the repair
Ask how long the workmanship guarantee on the repair lasts, in writing
For jobs of $3,000 or more in Knox County, verify the Home Improvement or contractor license
If the roof is near the end of its life, ask for a repair price and a replacement price

faqs.q: How much does a roof repair cost?
faqs.a: HomeAdvisor's June 2026 data puts the national average at about $1,174, with most repairs between $395 and $1,968. Simple fixes can start around $150, while extensive repairs can reach roughly $8,000. Leak repairs are listed at $360 to $1,550 and flashing repairs at $200 to $500. Knoxville prices depend on access, pitch and materials, so compare written quotes.

faqs.q: Can a roofer find a leak that only shows up in heavy rain?
faqs.a: Often, though it can take more than one visit. Roofers trace stains back through the attic, check the flashing and penetrations above the wet area, and sometimes water-test a section with a hose. A leak that appears only with wind-driven rain from one direction is often traced to flashing or a wall transition rather than the shingles themselves.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing a 20-year-old roof?
faqs.a: It depends on the shingle type and condition. InterNACHI estimates about 20 years for 3-tab shingles and about 30 for architectural shingles, so a 20-year-old architectural roof may have useful life left while a 3-tab roof of the same age may not. If the damage is isolated and the shingles are still flexible, a repair can buy time.

faqs.q: Will homeowners insurance pay for a roof repair?
faqs.a: That depends on the cause and your policy wording. Homeowners policies are typically written around sudden damage, such as a limb strike or wind tearing off shingles, rather than gradual wear. Photograph the damage first and read your policy or call your agent. TDCI advises filing claims promptly because policies may set notice deadlines.

name: Storm Damage Roof Repair
title: Storm & Hail Damage Roof Repair in Knoxville, TN
meta_description: Hail or wind damage to your Knoxville roof? Get free quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers for inspection and repair. No cost, no obligation.
h1: Storm Damage Roof Repair in Knoxville
hero_subtitle: After hail or high winds, get matched with up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers who can inspect the damage and quote the repair. There's no cost to you and no obligation to hire.
intro: Severe weather in East Tennessee follows a pattern. According to the National Weather Service office in Morristown, tornadoes peak in April, large hail peaks in May, and damaging thunderstorm winds take over in June, with a smaller second round of hail and tornadoes in November. Storm damage isn't always visible from the driveway, and the days after a storm are when unfamiliar crews start knocking on doors. Here's how to spot damage safely, document it, and hire carefully.

sections.heading: When storm season hits Knoxville
body: The NWS climatology for the Morristown forecast area also found that severe storms are most frequent in the afternoon, with a peak around 4 p.m. for tornadoes, hail and wind alike. If a line of storms crossed your neighborhood on a spring or summer afternoon, look over your roof once the weather clears, even if nothing obvious broke.

How much hail hurts a roof depends on the size of the stones and how long they fell. Wind damage tends to show up along ridges, rakes and eaves, where gusts get under a shingle and break its seal strip. Falling limbs can cause both kinds of damage at once and may crack decking or rafters.

sections.heading: What storm damage looks like
body: From the ground, look for missing shingles, shingles flipped back or creased across the middle, dented gutters and downspouts, and dings on mailboxes, roof vents or the tops of air-conditioning units. Fresh dents on soft metal are useful evidence that hail hit the property. Piles of granules at the downspout outlets after a storm are another sign.

Up close, a roofer looks for bruises where the shingle mat under the granules is fractured, for cracked or torn tabs, and for damage to vents and flashing. Many of these marks are hard to see without walking the roof, which is a job for a contractor with fall protection, not for a homeowner on a wet ladder.

sections.heading: Document first, then repair
body: Photograph and video the damage before anything is cleaned up; TDCI recommends this after every storm. If water is getting in, a tarp or temporary patch to prevent further damage is reasonable, and you should keep the receipts. Then report the claim to your insurer promptly, since many policies set deadlines for notice.

Tennessee's residential roofing law lets a roofer charge for emergency repairs that you acknowledge in writing as necessary to prevent damage to your home. The same law bars a roofer from misrepresenting that emergency repairs are needed, so get any emergency work described on paper before it starts.

sections.heading: Storm chasers and door-knockers
body: TDCI's post-storm advice has been consistent for years: be wary of contractors who solicit roof repairs door to door or by phone, don't sign anything on the spot, and don't pay cash or pay in full before the work is done. If a contractor needs money for materials, the department suggests going along and paying the supplier directly.

Check the license before you agree to anything. Storm work in Knox County priced from $3,000 to $24,999 needs a state Home Improvement license, and anything at $25,000 or more needs a contractor's license. TDCI also suggests writing down the contractor's vehicle plate and driver's license numbers.

sections.heading: Getting fair storm repair quotes
body: Ask each roofer to put the scope in writing with photos: which slopes are damaged, how many squares need replacing, and whether flashing, vents, gutters or decking are included. When an insurer is involved, compare the roofer's scope with the adjuster's estimate line by line so any differences can be raised before work begins.

A roofer who recommends replacement when the adjuster approved a repair isn't automatically wrong, but they should be able to show you why. If your insurer later tells you in writing that all or part of the claim isn't covered, Tennessee law gives you until midnight on the third business day after that notice to cancel the roofing contract.

Timing matters as well. After a widespread hailstorm, established local roofers can have long waiting lists, and that's when the pressure to sign quickly is highest. A tarp over a leaking section buys enough time to collect two or three written quotes instead of going with whoever knocked first.

checklist: Photograph the damage and note the storm date before any cleanup
Check gutters, downspouts, vents and AC units for fresh hail dents
Verify the roofer's Tennessee license before signing anything
Ask for photos of each damaged slope along with the written scope
Get any emergency tarp or patch work described in writing first
Don't pay cash, and don't pay in full before the job is finished
If a contractor came to your door, write down their plate and driver's license numbers

faqs.q: When is hail season in East Tennessee?
faqs.a: The National Weather Service office in Morristown found that large hail in its forecast area peaks in May, a little later than the April peak for tornadoes, with a slight secondary bump in November. Most hail events happen in the afternoon. Hail can fall in other months too, so check your roof after any strong storm.

faqs.q: Should I let a door-to-door roofer inspect my roof?
faqs.a: You can say no. TDCI specifically warns homeowners to be wary of contractors who go door to door offering roof repairs. If you do allow a look, don't sign anything that day, even a form described as a simple authorization, until you've read it fully, checked the license and gotten another opinion from a roofer you contacted yourself.

faqs.q: How long do I have to report storm damage to my insurer?
faqs.a: That's set by your policy, not by a single state deadline. TDCI notes that policies may require notice within a certain time, so check yours and report the damage as soon as you reasonably can. Give the insurer complete information and photos, since partial information can delay processing.

faqs.q: Can wind damage be fixed without replacing the whole roof?
faqs.a: Often, yes. If the damage is confined to a section and matching shingles are available, a repair may be enough. A roofer should also check whether nearby shingles have lost their seal, since unsealed shingles are more likely to blow off in the next storm. Ask for photos that show the extent of the damage.

name: Metal Roofing
title: Metal Roofing in Knoxville, TN | Free Installation Quotes
meta_description: Compare free metal roofing quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured Knoxville roofers. Standing seam or exposed-fastener panels, with no cost and no obligation.
h1: Metal Roofing Quotes in Knoxville, TN
hero_subtitle: Considering a metal roof? Get matched with up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers who install standing seam and exposed-fastener systems, and compare their quotes at no cost.
intro: A metal roof is a long-term decision. InterNACHI's life-expectancy chart puts metal roofing at 40 to 80 years, compared with roughly 20 to 30 for asphalt shingles, and the price reflects that. With spring hail, summer thunderstorm winds and humid summers in the Knoxville area, it's worth weighing metal against architectural shingles when your current roof wears out. This page compares standing seam and exposed-fastener systems, lists what 2026 cost guides report, and covers what to ask an installer.

sections.heading: Standing seam vs. exposed-fastener panels
body: Standing seam panels run from ridge to eave with raised seams that lock or snap together, and they're held down by clips or fasteners concealed under the seam. No screws pierce the face of the roof. The clips let panels expand and contract with temperature, which matters on a roof that swings between freezing winter nights and hot summer afternoons.

Exposed-fastener panels, often called screw-down, ribbed or corrugated panels, are fastened through the face with screws that carry rubber washers. They cost less to buy and install, but every screw is a potential leak point. Over the years washers can break down and screws can back out, so plan on periodic inspection and refastening.

A third option, metal shingles or shakes, is stamped to resemble asphalt, slate or wood while keeping the durability of metal. HomeAdvisor lists them at $7 to $22 per square foot installed. They can suit a street or homeowners association where a panel look would stand out.

sections.heading: What metal roofing costs
body: Guides published in 2026 give wide ranges because metal type, gauge, panel profile and roof complexity all move the price. Modernize's Tennessee guide reports $9 to $18 per square foot installed for most metal systems in the state, and $22,000 to $40,000 to put standing seam on a 2,000 square foot roof. Exposed-fastener panels come in lower; Roof Observations' 2026 steel guide puts them around $8.25 per square foot installed on average, versus about $12.75 for standing seam steel.
Steep pitches, multiple valleys and dormers, skylights and chimneys all add labor and trim pieces. The same panel can cost noticeably more on a complicated roof than on a simple gable.

National figures run even wider. HomeAdvisor's June 2026 data lists standing seam at $7 to $30 per square foot and corrugated sheets at $3.50 to $15. Ranges that broad are a reminder to compare quotes on the same panel, gauge and finish rather than on price per square alone.

sections.heading: How metal handles East Tennessee weather
body: Hail can dent metal panels. Some homeowners policies treat dents on metal as cosmetic and limit coverage for them, so ask your agent how your policy handles it before you choose a panel. Heavier-gauge metal resists denting better than thinner panels.

Moisture is the other consideration. Knoxville's average morning relative humidity runs around 85 percent, and condensation can form on the underside of metal panels when warm, damp air meets a cold surface. A suitable underlayment and good attic ventilation are part of a sound metal installation, not optional extras.

sections.heading: Installation details to ask about
body: Ask whether panels will go over solid decking with underlayment or over purlins, what gauge and paint system are being quoted, and whether the finish carries its own warranty against fading and chalking. On standing seam, ask whether panels are roll-formed on site or delivered pre-cut, and how long runs are allowed to move.

Trim and flashing are where metal roofs succeed or fail. Ridge caps, valleys, eave and rake trim, pipe boots and chimney flashing should be designed for the specific panel system. A crew that's excellent with shingles may have less experience with metal, so ask how many metal roofs they've installed and request addresses you can drive past.

sections.heading: Comparing metal roofing quotes
body: Make sure each quote names the panel profile, metal (steel or aluminum), gauge, finish system and color, along with the underlayment, fastener type and trim package. Two quotes that both say standing seam can describe very different products.

Licensing still applies. At the standing seam prices in Modernize's Tennessee guide, many full installations will reach $25,000, the point where Tennessee requires a state contractor's license. Below that, residential metal roofing jobs in Knox County from $3,000 to $24,999 fall under the state Home Improvement license.

cost_table.caption: Installed metal roofing costs reported in 2026 guides. Rough ranges, not quotes.
rows: Standing seam on a 2,000 sq ft roof in Tennessee

checklist: Get the panel profile, metal type and gauge in writing
Ask what paint system is used and whether it has its own fade and chalk warranty
Confirm the underlayment product and that it's suitable for use under metal
Ask how panel expansion is handled on long runs
Find out how the crew will flash chimneys, skylights and sidewalls
Ask your insurance agent how hail dents on metal are covered
Request addresses of metal roofs the contractor has installed
Verify the Tennessee license that matches the contract price

faqs.q: How long does a metal roof last?
faqs.a: InterNACHI's life-expectancy chart estimates 40 to 80 years for metal roofing, and HomeAdvisor cites 40 to 70 years for a well-installed metal roof. Actual life depends on the metal, the paint system, installation quality and upkeep. Exposed-fastener roofs need their screws and washers checked over time, while standing seam systems need less routine attention.

faqs.q: Does a metal roof cost more than shingles?
faqs.a: Yes, at the start. Modernize's 2026 Tennessee guide lists architectural shingles at $5 to $10.50 per square foot installed and most metal systems at $9 to $18. Over the life of the house the comparison narrows, because a metal roof can outlast two or more shingle roofs. How long you plan to stay in the home is a big part of the math.

faqs.q: Can metal go over my existing shingles?
faqs.a: Some installers will put metal over one layer of shingles where codes and the panel manufacturer allow it, often with battens or an added underlayment layer, while others insist on a tear-off. Ask each installer which method they're quoting, how it affects ventilation, and what the manufacturer requires to keep the warranty valid.

faqs.q: Standing seam or exposed fastener: which is better for a house?
faqs.a: Standing seam costs more but has no exposed screws and allows the panels to move with temperature changes, which reduces long-term maintenance. Exposed-fastener panels are the budget option and can work well on simpler roofs if you're prepared to inspect and replace fasteners over time. Get both priced for your roof before deciding.

name: Commercial Roofing
title: Commercial Roofing in Knoxville, TN | Compare Free Quotes
meta_description: Request free commercial roofing quotes for Knoxville offices, stores, churches and warehouses. Compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers with no obligation.
hero_subtitle: Building owners and property managers can request quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers for TPO, EPDM, modified bitumen and metal roofs. Free, with no obligation.
intro: Commercial buildings in the Knoxville area see the same weather as houses, but many sit under flat or low-slope roofs where drains and scuppers, not steep pitch, have to move water off. Rooftop HVAC units add penetrations and foot traffic, and a leak can interrupt a business as well as damage a ceiling. This page covers the main membrane systems, what national guides report for installed cost and expected life, how Tennessee licensing applies to commercial work, and how to compare commercial bids.

sections.heading: Low-slope systems you'll be quoted
body: TPO is a single-ply membrane, usually white, with heat-welded seams. EPDM is a black synthetic rubber membrane that's typically adhered, mechanically fastened or ballasted, with seams joined by tape or adhesive. Modified bitumen is an asphalt-based sheet applied in layers, and built-up roofing (BUR) alternates layers of felt and asphalt, often finished with gravel. Metal panels are also an option on buildings with enough slope to shed water.

InterNACHI's life-expectancy chart gives broad ranges: 7 to 20 years for TPO, 15 to 25 for EPDM, about 20 for modified bitumen and about 30 for built-up roofing. Membrane thickness, attachment method, insulation and maintenance push a given roof toward one end of its range or the other.

sections.heading: Flat-roof trouble spots in this climate
body: With about 52 inches of precipitation in a normal year at Knoxville, drainage is the first thing to look at. Water that ponds for days after a rain, clogged drains and gutters, and debris built up around scuppers all shorten a membrane's life. Summer heat and sun also work on seams and flashings, especially around rooftop equipment.

Many commercial leaks start at penetrations: HVAC curbs, pipe stacks, exhaust fans, skylights and parapet walls all rely on flashing details. Technicians walking to rooftop units can puncture a membrane, so ask about walkway pads along regular service routes.

Routine inspections catch many of these problems while they're still small. Building owners often have a commercial roof checked in spring and fall and after major storms, with drains cleared and the flashing at equipment curbs looked over each time. A simple log of leaks, repairs and inspection photos also helps with warranty claims and with budgeting for the eventual replacement.

sections.heading: Repair, restore or replace
body: A commercial roof doesn't always need a full tear-off. A localized leak can be patched, and a roof with dry, sound insulation may be a candidate for a coating or a recover system, where a new membrane goes over the existing one. Wet insulation is often the deciding factor, because sealing it under a new roof causes problems later. Ask each roofer how they'll check for it; infrared scans and core cuts are common methods.

When full replacement is due, the job typically includes removing the old membrane and any wet insulation, adding new insulation and cover board, and installing new membrane, edge metal and flashing. Work hours, staging areas, equipment disconnects and tenant notices belong in the plan.

sections.heading: Licensing and bidding in Tennessee
body: Tennessee requires a state contractor's license before anyone bids or negotiates a price on a project of $25,000 or more, and roofing subcontractors need one when their share of a project reaches $25,000. The Board for Licensing Contractors lists roofing as classification BC-21. Each license carries a monetary limit, so confirm the contractor's limit covers the size of your job.

The state Home Improvement license applies to residential remodeling, so it doesn't cover a storefront or office. For commercial jobs under $25,000, TDCI suggests checking with your local building codes office about license and permit requirements. Ask every bidder for a certificate of insurance listing your company as the certificate holder.

sections.heading: Comparing commercial roofing bids
body: Commercial bids can look alike and still differ a lot. Line them up by membrane type and thickness (for example, 45-mil versus 60-mil TPO), attachment method, insulation thickness and R-value, cover board, tapered insulation for drainage, edge metal, and how many drains and curbs are being reflashed.

Read the warranty terms closely. A manufacturer's system warranty, a materials-only warranty and the contractor's own workmanship warranty are different documents with different conditions. Ask what the manufacturer requires in inspections and maintenance to keep coverage in force.

cost_table.caption: Installed low-slope roofing costs from 2026 national guides, with InterNACHI life estimates. These guides are largely residential; commercial pricing varies with size, insulation and access.

checklist: Confirm the contractor's Tennessee license, classification and monetary limit at search.cloud.commerce.tn.gov
Request a certificate of insurance naming your company as certificate holder
Ask how wet insulation will be found and how replacing it is priced
Compare membrane type, thickness and attachment method across bids
Ask which drains, curbs and penetrations will be reflashed
Get the manufacturer warranty type, length and maintenance requirements
Agree on work hours, staging areas and how rooftop equipment will be handled

faqs.q: How long does a commercial flat roof last?
faqs.a: InterNACHI estimates 7 to 20 years for TPO, 15 to 25 for EPDM, about 20 for modified bitumen and about 30 for built-up roofing. Thicker membranes, good drainage and regular inspections, especially around rooftop equipment, help a roof reach the upper end. Ponding water and neglected penetrations pull it toward the lower end.

faqs.q: Can a new roof go over our existing commercial roof?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A recover system or coating can work when the existing roof and insulation are dry and sound, and it avoids the cost and disruption of a full tear-off. If moisture is trapped in the insulation, covering it usually causes problems later. Ask bidders to explain how they tested for moisture and what codes allow for your building.

faqs.q: What license does a commercial roofer need in Tennessee?
faqs.a: For any project of $25,000 or more, Tennessee requires a state contractor's license before bidding, and roofing subcontractors need one when their portion reaches $25,000. Roofing is classification BC-21. Licenses carry a monetary limit, so check that it covers your job. For smaller commercial jobs, ask your local codes office about local licensing.

faqs.q: Is requesting quotes free for businesses?
faqs.a: Yes. There's no charge to request quotes and no obligation to hire. Local roofing contractors pay for the referral, and you'll hear from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers, usually within 24 to 48 hours. Describing the building, roof type and any active leaks in your request helps them prepare.

h1: Roof Insurance Claims in Knoxville, TN
hero_subtitle: Learn how a roof damage claim works in Tennessee and what roofers can and can't do, then get free repair or replacement quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers.
intro: A roof claim involves three parties: you, your insurance company and the roofer who does the work. Tennessee has a law written for exactly that situation. Since 2012, residential roofing contracts expected to be paid from an insurance claim must include written disclosures and give you a way out if your insurer denies all or part of the claim. This page walks through the claim process, explains those protections in plain language, and covers what to watch for when a contractor offers to handle the claim for you.

sections.heading: How a roof claim usually unfolds
body: Start by documenting the damage with photos and video and protecting the house from more water. Then report the claim. TDCI points out that policies may set deadlines for notice and that giving your insurer only partial information delays processing. The insurer assigns an adjuster, who inspects the roof and writes an estimate.

Once you have that estimate, get roofing quotes for the same scope. If a roofer finds damage the adjuster missed, TDCI's guidance is to contact your insurance company to resolve the difference. If you have a mortgage, the lender may be named on the check or may hold structural repair money in escrow and release it as work is completed.

sections.heading: Tennessee's residential roofing contract law
body: Under Tennessee Code sections 62-6-601 through 62-6-604, a roofer whose contract is expected to be paid from insurance must give you certain information in writing before you sign: a business mailing address, a phone number, any contractor, home improvement or public adjuster license numbers held in any state, an email or fax for cancellations, and a detailed description of the damage and repairs. The contract also has to carry a boldface cancellation notice and a detachable cancellation form.

If your insurer later tells you in writing that all or part of the claim isn't covered, you can cancel by notifying the roofer before midnight on the third business day after you receive that notice. Until coverage is confirmed in writing or that window closes, the roofer can't require payment, and after a valid cancellation must refund your money within 10 business days, apart from emergency repairs you approved in writing.

sections.heading: Roofers, adjusters and who speaks for you
body: Your roofer can meet the adjuster at the house, point out damage and supply photos and measurements; TDCI's own guidance mentions having your contractor meet with you and the adjuster. Negotiating the claim on your behalf is a different role. In Tennessee, no one may act or hold out as a public adjuster without a license from the Department of Commerce and Insurance.

If you want professional help with a disputed claim, a licensed public adjuster represents you and is usually paid a percentage of the settlement. TDCI recommends confirming the license, asking for references and getting fees in writing. Read every page of any document that would give a contractor control over your claim or your insurance payments before you sign it.

sections.heading: About your deductible
body: Your deductible is the share of the loss your policy assigns to you, and it's subtracted from what the insurer pays. If a roofer offers to cover, absorb or waive it, ask exactly how the numbers work. The money has to come from somewhere, and one way is an inflated estimate sent to your insurer under your name. Talk to your insurer or agent before agreeing to any arrangement like that.

Some policies also pay in stages, with part of the money held back until repairs are finished. Ask your adjuster how your policy handles this so the payment schedule in your roofing contract lines up with when insurance funds actually arrive.

sections.heading: If your claim is denied or underpaid
body: Ask the insurer to explain the decision in writing and point to the policy language it relied on. You can request a re-inspection, send in a roofer's photos and estimate, or ask whether your policy has an appraisal provision for settling disputes over the amount of a loss.

If you still disagree, TDCI can mediate complaints about policies written in Tennessee; the department lists 615-741-2218 and 1-800-342-4029. And if a denial arrives after you've signed a roofing contract, remember that the three-business-day cancellation window starts when you receive the insurer's written notice.

checklist: Photograph and video all damage before cleanup or repairs
Report the claim promptly and note the claim number and adjuster's name
Ask for the written disclosures Tennessee law requires before you sign
Make sure the contract includes the cancellation notice and detachable form
Compare the roofer's scope with the adjuster's estimate line by line
Verify any public adjuster's license with the Department of Commerce and Insurance
Read in full anything that would give a contractor control of your claim

faqs.q: Can my roofer deal with my insurance company for me?
faqs.a: A roofer can document damage, attend the adjuster's inspection and provide photos, measurements and an estimate. Negotiating the claim on your behalf is the job of a public adjuster, and Tennessee requires public adjusters to be licensed by the Department of Commerce and Insurance. Ask anyone offering to handle your claim for their license number.

faqs.q: What if my insurer denies the claim after I've signed with a roofer?
faqs.a: Tennessee law lets you cancel a roofing contract tied to an insurance claim if the insurer tells you in writing that all or part of the claim isn't covered. Your signed, dated cancellation must reach the roofer before midnight on the third business day after you receive that notice. Payments are refunded within 10 business days, except for approved emergency repairs.

faqs.q: Should I get roofing quotes before or after the adjuster visits?
faqs.a: Either can work. An early inspection from a roofer can help you decide whether the damage is likely to exceed your deductible before you file. Having a roofer present during the adjuster's visit can also help make sure damage isn't missed. Either way, compare quotes against the adjuster's written estimate.

faqs.q: Will this site help me file my insurance claim?
faqs.a: No. This site connects homeowners with local roofers for free quotes; it doesn't file claims, negotiate with insurers or act as an adjuster. Your insurance company, your agent or a licensed public adjuster are the right contacts for claim questions. The roofers you're matched with can document damage and quote the repair.

h1: Emergency Roof Repair in Knoxville, TN
hero_subtitle: Water through the ceiling or a tree on the roof? Start with safety, then request quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured local roofers, who usually reach out within 24 to 48 hours.
intro: Roof emergencies rarely happen at a convenient time. A limb comes down in a summer thunderstorm, wind peels back a section of shingles, or a slow leak suddenly soaks through a ceiling in a heavy rain. In the first few hours the goals are simple: keep people safe, stop more water from getting in, and document everything for your insurer. This page covers what to do right away, what a temporary repair should involve, and how Tennessee law treats emergency roofing charges.

sections.heading: First steps when water is coming in
body: Safety comes first. If water is near light fixtures, outlets or the electrical panel, shut off power to that area at the breaker if you can reach it safely, and keep everyone out of rooms where the ceiling is sagging. A ceiling bulging with water can be relieved by poking a small hole at the lowest point over a bucket, which keeps the water from spreading across the drywall.

Move furniture and electronics, put down towels and containers, and take photos and video of the damage inside and anything visible outside. Stay off a wet or storm-damaged roof. A fall is a far bigger risk than the leak, and a roofer has the equipment to work up there safely.

sections.heading: Temporary repairs: tarps and patches
body: The usual short-term fix is a heavy tarp over the damaged area, secured with wood battens and carried over the ridge where possible so water can't run under its top edge. A roofer may also install a temporary patch or seal around a broken vent or torn flashing until a permanent repair can be scheduled. A tarp is meant to last weeks, not seasons; sun and wind break it down, so book the permanent fix rather than living under blue plastic.

Ask what the temporary work will cost before it starts, and keep the receipt. Homeowners policies commonly expect you to protect the property from further damage, and reasonable costs for doing so are often part of the claim. Check your policy wording or ask your agent.

sections.heading: Emergency charges under Tennessee law
body: Tennessee's residential roofing law treats emergency work separately when a roofing contract is expected to be paid by insurance. The roofer can charge for emergency repairs you acknowledge in writing as necessary to prevent damage to your property, and that charge stands even if you later cancel the main contract after an insurance denial.

The same statute prohibits a roofer from misrepresenting that emergency repairs are needed. If someone at your door insists the whole roof has to be replaced tonight, slow down. A legitimate emergency visit focuses on stopping water, with the permanent repair or replacement quoted separately.

sections.heading: Typical emergencies around Knoxville
body: Summer thunderstorms are a likely culprit: the NWS office in Morristown found that wind damage becomes the dominant type of severe weather in its area in June, and that storms peak in the afternoon. Large hail peaks earlier, in May, and spring systems can bring both hail and wind.

Winter brings its own problems. Knoxville averages only about 4.6 inches of snow a year, yet the NWS period-of-record average is about 68 nights at or below freezing. Ice in clogged gutters or valleys can back water up under shingles at the eaves, so leaks that appear only during a thaw often trace back there.

sections.heading: After the emergency: the permanent fix
body: Once the house is dry and the damage is contained, get written quotes for the permanent repair. The roofer who tarped the house isn't automatically the right choice for the full job, and a second quote is reasonable. Before you sign, check the license on the state's search site; in Knox County, home repairs priced from $3,000 up to $25,000 call for a Home Improvement license.

If drywall, insulation or flooring got wet, ask whether the roofer's scope covers any of it or whether you'll need a separate contractor for drying and interior repairs. Wet materials left in place can grow mold, so don't let that part wait.

Even in a hurry, the usual payment rules apply. TDCI advises against paying in cash or paying the full price up front, and notes that state law limits home improvement deposits to one-third of the contract price. Photograph the finished work before the final payment.

checklist: Shut off power to wet areas if you can reach the breaker safely
Photograph interior and exterior damage before cleanup
Ask the price of tarping or temporary repairs before work begins
Get any emergency work described and acknowledged in writing
Keep receipts for tarps, fans, buckets and other mitigation costs
Call your insurer to report the damage and ask about next steps
Get separate written quotes for the permanent repair

faqs.q: Should I tarp my roof myself?
faqs.a: Only if you can do it safely from a ladder on a low, dry roof in calm weather, and even then a second person should hold the ladder. A wet, steep or storm-damaged roof is dangerous, and a fall costs far more than a leak. Containing water inside and calling a roofer is usually the better choice.

faqs.q: Will insurance pay for emergency tarping?
faqs.a: It may, depending on your policy and the cause of the damage. Policies commonly expect you to take reasonable steps to prevent further damage, so keep receipts and photos of the temporary work. Report the claim promptly; TDCI notes that policies may set deadlines for notice.

faqs.q: How fast will a roofer respond?
faqs.a: Roofers you're matched with through this site usually reach out within 24 to 48 hours. After a widespread storm, local crews can be booked up, so if water is actively coming in, contain it inside, call your insurer, and keep documenting the damage while you wait.

faqs.q: Can a roofer charge me for emergency work if I cancel the contract?
faqs.a: Under Tennessee's residential roofing law, yes, for emergency repairs you acknowledged in writing as necessary to prevent damage. Other payments must be refunded within 10 business days if you validly cancel after an insurance denial. The law also forbids a roofer from claiming emergency repairs are necessary when they aren't.
